'''Michael Bahr''' is credited with the original concept of two Players Committee [[Virtual cards]].<ref name="cardlabels">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/src/gemp-swccg-cards/src/main/resources/card_labels.json card_labels.json] in billbisco/swccg-gemp (commit 0bc4377d9): the printed labels of every Players Committee Virtual card, transcribed from the PC's card images (res.starwarsccg.org). Field definitions: [https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/docs/card_labels.md docs/card_labels.md].</ref> The concept credit names where the concept was won: PC Volunteer Award 2006. The cards are in [[Virtual Block 4]] (cards first released 2002–2009) and [[Virtual Set 0]] (released 24 September 2014).

In August 2006 the Players Committee Design Team had a long discussion with Bahr and [[Jim Colson]] about card availability and the cards that would one day be unavailable. At [[Scott Lingrell]]'s request Bahr then drew up a list of cards the Committee should avoid virtualizing. The result was the ''Star Wars CCG Virtualization Market Guide'' (version 2.0, 15 August 2006), which gave every card in the game a value from 1 (lowest, for example Jabba's Palace cards) to 12 (highest, Queen Amidala), with a list of the top cards that should never be virtualized and an "EPP caveat". From [[Virtual Set 16: Revenge Of The Sith|Virtual Set 16]] the Design Team used that top list when deciding which cards to virtualize; the Committee published the guide's text on 15 August 2008.<ref name="pc-sid94">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=94 Policy of virtualizing], swccgpc.com (15 August 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080906211140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=94 Internet Archive]</ref> In October 2008 Lingrell credited "Mike Bahr and others" for much of what the Committee had learned about design.<ref name="pc-lingrell08">[http://www.swccgpc.com/news/news.php?id=7 10 Questions with Scott Lingrell], swccgpc.com (8 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081009225918/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/news/news.php?id=7 Internet Archive]</ref>
